transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess things at work just got a bit... out of hand. I'm a production manager, and for a while, I was just doing a lot. I was launching all these plant redesign projects, calling our suppliers well after hours... I even rewrote the entire shift plan by myself. But... lately, I just... I can't keep up with any of it. The very plans I set in motion, I just... I can't do it anymore. So... I guess that's why I'm here.
How long did that period of intense energy, extra projects, and reduced need for sleep last before things changed?
Um... I'm not really sure. I didn't exactly keep track of the days. It was just... a while, I guess. Before everything sort of... stopped.
How long has this current period of low energy and difficulty keeping up with things been going on?
Um... about three months, I think. It's just been... a really heavy stretch. And, um... with the move and the plant assignment... it just made it all much harder to manage.

During that period when you were taking on all those extra projects and needed less sleep, did coworkers or family notice a clear change in you, or did it cause any significant problems at work or in your relationships?

Um... I don't know. People might have thought I was just... working hard. I don't really talk to my family about work. And... I don't think I got into trouble or anything, if that's what you mean. I just... did a lot of work.
Thinking back to that period when you were taking on extra projects and needed less sleep, can you tell me roughly how many days in a row that lasted before it stopped?
I really couldn't give you a number. Um... it's hard to look back and just... count them. It was a continuous stretch, but I didn't mark it on a calendar or anything. I just... I don't know exactly.
During that period when you were taking on extra projects and needed less sleep, did you notice your mood itself feeling unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable—different from your normal self?

Um... I suppose. At the beginning of that assignment, I felt... I don't know, almost electrically upbeat, I guess. But then... it just turned into feeling weirdly irritable. Like... if anyone questioned my ideas, it just felt like they were slowing down something obvious. And important. So... yeah, I guess my mood was a bit different.
Even though you didn't count exact days, would you say that period of feeling unusually upbeat and then irritable lasted at least four days in a row, or was it shorter than that?
I... I don't really know. Like I said, I didn't count. It felt like a while, but... I couldn't tell you if it was exactly four days. It's just hard to remember.

During that time when you felt unusually upbeat and then irritable, did you notice yourself feeling more confident or important than usual—like your ideas or abilities were especially superior to others'?

I mean... I guess I felt pretty sure of myself. Um... I just remember thinking I could fix the whole production workflow. Like, faster than the entire consulting team they brought in. People had concerns, but I just... brushed them off. It just didn't seem possible that I could fail. So... yeah, I suppose I felt more confident.
During that period of high energy and confidence, did it ever get so intense that it caused serious problems at work, led to any risky decisions, or required someone to intervene or hospitalize you?
Um... no. Nothing like that. I mean... I didn't get fired or anything, and I definitely wasn't in a hospital. It wasn't... it didn't get to that point.

During that period when you felt unusually upbeat and then irritable, did anyone close to you—like a coworker, friend, or family member—actually comment that you seemed different from your usual self?
Um... I don't think so. I mean... nobody really said anything to me directly. I don't know what they were thinking, but... no one brought it up.

You mentioned this happened during your plant assignment—do you remember roughly how long that assignment lasted, like a few days, a couple of weeks, or longer, that might help us pin down how long you were feeling that upbeat and irritable?
I don't really remember exactly. Um... maybe a week or two? I was just focused on the work, so I wasn't really keeping track of the days.

During that week or two of feeling unusually upbeat and then irritable, did you notice an actual change in how you were functioning at work—like taking on much more than usual or making decisions differently than you normally would?
Um... no, not really. I mean... I was just working. I don't think I was doing anything out of the ordinary, really. Just... doing my job.

During that week or two when you felt upbeat and then irritable, did you actually feel rested and full of energy after only a few hours of sleep, or were you just choosing to stay up later to get work done?

Um... I don't know if it was a choice, really. I just... I was sleeping maybe two or three hours a night. And I'd still go in to the plant feeling... fine. Sharp, even. It just felt like I didn't need it. Like sleep was just... inefficient, I guess. So I just didn't do it much.

During that week or two when you felt unusually upbeat and irritable, did you notice your thoughts racing or jumping quickly from one idea to another, or did you find yourself talking more than usual?

Um... I guess so. In meetings... I noticed I was talking a lot. Faster, too. I'd start talking about line speeds, and then... jump to staffing, and then supplier issues. Just... all at once. Before anyone else could really say anything. I just had a lot to get through.
